questions.question: If an object has two forces of equal size acting on it in opposite directions, what can we say about these forces?
options: They are unbalanced.
They are balanced.
They are contact forces.
They are magnetic forces.

questions.question: How do you calculate the resultant force acting on an object?
options: By multiplying the largest force by the smallest force.
By dividing the total mass by the sum of all forces.
By taking the sum of the forces, taking into account their direction.
By averaging all the forces acting on the object.

questions.question: If a toy car has a force of 10 N pushing it forward and a force of 4 N pulling it backward, in which direction does the resultant force act?
options: In the direction of the smaller force (backward).
Upward, perpendicular to both forces.
There is no direction because the forces cancel out.
In the direction of the bigger force (forward).

questions.question: What is the effect of increasing the size of the resultant force acting on a moving bicycle?
options: The bicycle will change its speed greater or faster.
The bicycle's mass will immediately increase.
The bicycle will continue at exactly the same constant speed.
The friction force will instantly drop to zero.

questions.question: Which of the following is a list of recognized stores of energy that an object can have?
options: Speed, friction, gravity, balance, and weight.
Light, sound, electrical, magnetic, and nuclear.
Gravitational, thermal, elastic, chemical, and kinetic.
Push, pull, twist, friction, and drag.

questions.question: What is the scientific definition of friction?
options: The downward pull of the Earth on an object's mass.
The force of one surface gripping or rubbing on another.
The upward push of a liquid on a floating object.
The force that keeps planets in orbit around the Sun.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of adding a lubricant, such as oil, between two moving metal surfaces?
options: To increase the chemical energy stored in the metal.
To increase the mass of the moving parts.
To make the surfaces grip each other more tightly.
To reduce the friction between the two surfaces.

questions.question: Which scientific instrument is used to measure the size of a force?
options: A newton meter
A thermometer
A voltmeter
A balance scale

questions.question: What is the standard unit of measurement for force?
options: Kilograms (kg)
Joules (J)
Newtons (N)
Metres per second (m/s)

questions.question: How do categoric variables differ from continuous variables in a science experiment?
options: Categoric variables only measure time, while continuous variables measure distance.
Categoric variables come in distinct types, while continuous variables can take any value on a numerical scale.
Categoric variables can take any numerical value, while continuous variables have no units.
Categoric variables are always kept the same, while continuous variables are what we change.

questions.question: To ensure a test is fair, what must we do with the variables we are not testing?
options: Keep them the same for every measurement.
Change them randomly after each trial.
Double their values for each subsequent test.
Remove them entirely from the experiment.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a contact force?
options: It can act even when objects are far apart.
It only exists in outer space.
It only acts when objects are touching.
It does not require any energy to be transferred.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of non-contact forces, such as gravity or magnetism?
options: They can act with or without the objects touching.
They only act when two surfaces are rubbing together.
They only exist when objects are in direct physical contact.
They cannot cause any change in an object's motion.

questions.question: What is drag?
options: A non-contact force that pulls objects toward the centre of the Earth.
A contact force that pushes against objects moving through liquids or gases.
The force of a surface supporting an object resting on it.
The energy stored in a stretched elastic band.

questions.question: When drawing force diagrams, what does the length of a force arrow represent?
options: The duration of time the force acts.
The mass of the object experiencing the force.
The size of the force.
The speed at which the object is moving.

questions.question: Why does a heavy loaded lorry require a larger force to stop than a small, light car?
options: Objects with a greater mass need a greater force to stop them moving.
Heavy objects always experience zero friction from the road.
The lorry has a smaller contact area with the ground.
Light cars do not have any kinetic energy store when moving.

questions.question: In physics, what is the fundamental definition of a force?
options: The rate of doing work.
The amount of matter inside an object.
A push or a pull.
The temperature of a substance.
